##Here is my MIMARKS data
```{r echo=FALSE}
# This is a piece of R code has been provided for you to insert your 
# MIMARKS template into # your report after you fill it out. Use Excel 
# to fill out Lab1-Mimarks.csv with your 
# metadata, and save this file as a .csv when you are finished. Do not 
# change this piece of code or your markdown will break.

library(knitr)
library(kableExtra)
options(knitr.table.format = "html")
template<-read.csv("~/Micro336-master/Templates/Lab1-Mimarks.csv")
template %>%
  kable() %>%
   kable_styling(bootstrap_options = "striped", full_width = F, font_size=7) %>%
   row_spec(0, angle = -45) %>%
  column_spec(1, border_right = T, width="8em") %>%
  column_spec(2, width = "6em") %>%
   column_spec(3, width = "5em") %>%
   column_spec(4, width = "5em") %>%
   column_spec(5, width = "5em") %>%
   column_spec(6, width = "5em")
```

##Here is my quantified DNA
```{r echo=FALSE}
# This is a piece of R code has been provided for you to insert your DNA 
# quantification data  into your report after you fill it out. Use Excel to 
# fill out Lab1-DNA.csv withyour DNA quantity data and save this file as a 
# .csv when you are finished. Do not change this piece of code or your markdown 
# will break.
library(ggplot2)
options(knitr.table.format = "html")
template2<-read.csv("~/Micro336-master/Templates/Lab1-DNA.csv")
mysub<-subset(template2, template2$source %in% c("serial1", "serial2"))
ggplot(mysub, aes(x=nanodrop.ng.ul, y=-log(dilution, 10), colour=source)) + geom_point() + ggtitle("Nanodrop serial dilutions") + ylab("Dilution factor (-log10)")
ggplot(mysub, aes(x=qubit.ng.ul, y=-log(dilution, 10), colour=source)) + geom_point() + ggtitle("Qubit serial dilutions") + ylab("Dilution factor (-log10)")

template2 %>%
  kable() %>%
   kable_styling(bootstrap_options = "striped", full_width = F, font_size=7) %>%
   row_spec(0, angle = -45) %>%
  column_spec(1, border_right = T, width="8em") %>%
  column_spec(2, width = "6em") %>%
   column_spec(3, width = "5em") %>%
   column_spec(4, width = "5em") %>%
   column_spec(5, width = "5em") %>%
     column_spec(6, width = "5em") %>%
   column_spec(7, width = "5em")

```
